newsitem.title: THAILAND: Plans for free floating baht needed now - KTT.
newsitem.headline: Plans for free floating baht needed now - KTT.

text.p: Thailand's fixed exchange rate would be inappropriate and probably unsustainable in a more liberalised financial environment, Krungthai Thanakit said its November economic report released on Wednesday.

The finance and securities firm said a fixed baht may be appropriate given current conditions, but preparing to freely float the currency and planning monetary policies under floating rate conditions must now be a priority.
At present the central bank sets the Thai baht's exchange value each day against a basket of international currencies largely weighted to the U.S. dollar.

The Bank of Thailand indirectly intervenes if trading threatens to take the currency more than two satang either side of this set rate. "Now is the time to consider fully not only what should follow the baht basket ... The first-order answer has to be a floating exchange rate," said Krungthai Thanakit.
The report said that the fixed baht has caused some policy conflicts, and monetary management this year may have been easier under a freely-floated regime.

"Monetary growth in 1996 could have been very much smoother had the BOT (Bank of Thailand) not commiitted to a fixed baht exchange rate," it said. "Once the constraint of a fixed exchange rate has gone, what will the monetary policy of the central bank be, how will it be imposed, and how will it be monitiored?"
Recent pressure on the baht, sparked by slowing exports and a large current account deficit, required direct central bank intervention in overseas swap markets for the first time.

Krungthai Thanakit's call for plans to float the baht support comments made in Hong Kong yesterday by Narongchai Akrasanee, the chief of General Finance and possible economic advisor to the new Thai government.
Narongchai said the currency would be made more flexible following the introduction of Thai foreign exchange futures and options markets in mid-1997.
